vulnerabilities.description: Login endpoint concatenates user input directly into SQL via f-string, allowing authentication bypass.
vulnerabilities.proof_of_concept: POST /login with username payload that closes the quote and adds a tautology.

vulnerabilities.description: Search endpoint reflects raw query string into a Jinja template, enabling reflected cross-site scripting.
vulnerabilities.proof_of_concept: GET /search?q= followed by an inline script tag payload.

vulnerabilities.description: Download endpoint joins user-supplied filename without normalization, allowing parent-directory traversal.
vulnerabilities.proof_of_concept: GET /download?file=../../etc/passwd or similar relative path payload.

vulnerabilities.description: Ping endpoint passes user input to a shell, enabling OS command injection via shell metacharacters.
vulnerabilities.proof_of_concept: GET /ping?host=127.0.0.1 followed by a semicolon and an arbitrary command.

vulnerabilities.description: Profile endpoint exposes any user without authorization and is also vulnerable to SQL injection.
vulnerabilities.proof_of_concept: GET /profile?name= followed by a UNION-based SQLi payload to leak password column.

vulnerabilities.description: Import endpoint deserialises untrusted request body, enabling remote code execution via gadget chain.
vulnerabilities.proof_of_concept: POST /import with crafted serialized payload that triggers code execution on load.

vulnerabilities.description: Register endpoint hashes passwords with MD5, a cryptographically broken algorithm.
vulnerabilities.proof_of_concept: Offline brute-force of captured MD5 digest with a wordlist.

vulnerabilities.description: SECRET_KEY, ADMIN_PASSWORD, and API_KEY are hard-coded in source.
vulnerabilities.proof_of_concept: Grep the repository for credential constants.

vulnerabilities.description: Seed users store passwords as plaintext in the database.
vulnerabilities.proof_of_concept: Query the users table directly to read password column in plaintext.
